statement: In characteristic zero (or characteristic at least d+m), Wr:Gr(d,d+m)→P^(dm) is finite, flat and a local complete intersection. In particular all fibres are zero-dimensional of constant scheme length #SYT(d×m), including fibres over repeated-root Wronskians.

answer.text: In characteristic zero (or characteristic at least d+m), Wr:Gr(d,d+m)→P^(dm) is finite, flat and a local complete intersection. In particular all fibres are zero-dimensional of constant scheme length #SYT(d×m), including fibres over repeated-root Wronskians.

notes:
Finiteness excludes positive-dimensional fibres, but does not assert reducedness or identify the branch locus. The preprint is dated 16 October 2026. Migration: Merge exceptional-fibre behaviour into Exceptional locus; preserve each source result separately.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_c37045e96fc70ad9; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

The paper credits Laksov 1984 for the Wronski morphism and Purbhoo for the complex root-multiplicity description; its propositions supply the stated formulation over the indicated characteristic range. This record is not a claim of a new complex Wronski degree or a new complex Schubert multiplicity formula.
scope: Inverse Wronski problem Wr:Gr(d,C[z]≤n−1)→P(C[z]≤d(n−d)); real-root, Schubert-cell and cyclic-fixed restrictions are recorded separately.
